annotations.title: Great shal be the glorie.
annotations.text: [1] When according to the prophets exhortation the temple was built againe, Esdras ch. 3. v 12. writeth, that such ancient men as had sene the former, lamented, because this new one was not so excellent as the former had bene, which is also clere by other places of holie scripture. For amongst other differences, Salomons temple had in height, and in breadth, an hundred and twentie cubites 2 Paral. 3. v. 4. this new temple had but sixtie cubites. 1 Esd. 6. v 3. Likewise Salomons temple was built of stones hewed and perfectly polished, 3. Reg 6. v. 7. which were also couered on the innerside with seeling worke of ceder wood. v 18. This new temple was built of rugh and vnpolished stones. 1. Esd. 5. v. 8 As for the same temple long after enlarged and adorned by Herod, it continued not long in that state, [2] & the chiefest glorie therof was by our Sauiours presence therin, when he was presented by his mother, and ioyfully receiued into the armes of Simeon, and often preached there. And therfore S. Augustin proueth li. 18. c. 45 ciuit. that the prophet here foresheweth the glorie of Christs mystical temple, faithful Christian soules of al nations, in whom God dwelleth by grace of the new Testament, farre more glorious in liuing stones, then that temple which king Salomon built, or that which was restored after the captiuitie.

notes.text: The temple restored after the captiuitie was not so glorious as that which Salomon built.
But Christs Church of the new Testament in which he dwelleth spiritually farre excelleth the material temple.
